traditional_uses: Supports sleep and stress resilience as a medhya rasayana
Used in kshaya-vasa (wasting and respiratory) conditions
plants.typical_dosage: Churna 3-6 g/day; Kashaya 10-20 ml; tablets per standardized label
plants.safety_notes: Avoid in pregnancy, hyperthyroidism, and autoimmune disease without supervision. May cause GI upset at high doses.
plants.ip_notes: A US patent on an extraction method was revoked (2005) after TKDL-based prior-art review. Major export crop; benefit-sharing debates continue under the Biological Diversity Act.

traditional_uses: Wound healing and skin conditions (vranya, kustha)
Food preservative, dye, and ritual use across India
plants.typical_dosage: Churna 1-3 g/day; curcuminoid extracts per standardized label
plants.safety_notes: High doses may aggravate gallbladder disease; possible anticoagulant interaction.
plants.gi_status: Alleppey Turmeric and Erode Turmeric are GI-registered in India
plants.ip_notes: Landmark case: the US patent on turmeric's wound-healing use was revoked in 1997 after CSIR demonstrated prior art from Sanskrit and Urdu texts - the founding moment of TKDL.

traditional_uses: Respiratory support in cough, cold, and shwasa
plants.typical_dosage: Leaf churna 3-6 g/day; fresh leaves as dietary use
plants.safety_notes: Anti-fertility effects seen in high-dose animal studies; caution with anticoagulants.
plants.ip_notes: TKDL documentation of Tulasi's respiratory uses has been cited to block novelty claims on aqueous-extract therapeutic patents.

plants.typical_dosage: Seed powder 5-10 g/day; soaked seeds as food
plants.safety_notes: Uterotonic at large doses - avoid medicinally in pregnancy. Maple-like odor in sweat is benign.
plants.ip_notes: TKDL records of fenugreek use for glucose metabolism were cited against EPO/US applications claiming the same therapeutic utility.

plants.botanical_name: Terminalia arjuna (Roxb. ex DC.) Wight & Arn.
traditional_uses: Lipid and vascular health in modern adjunct use
plants.safety_notes: Generally well tolerated; theoretical additive effect with cardiac glycosides and antihypertensives.
plants.ip_notes: Classical cardiac indications documented in Charaka Sushruta are indexed in TKDL and used as prior art in pharma patent examination.

traditional_uses: Sore throat, cough, hoarseness (kasa, swara bheda)
plants.safety_notes: Prolonged high doses cause pseudohyperaldosteronism: hypertension, hypokalemia, edema. Avoid in kidney disease.
plants.ip_notes: Standardized deglycyrrhizinated extract processes are patented internationally; raw-traditional-use art is in TKDL.

rasa: Pancha-rasa (all five tastes except tikta per some texts; classically amla/kashaya/madhura/lavana/ksara)
plants.prabhava: Rasayana par excellence; highest natural vitamin-C food
traditional_uses: Core ingredient of Triphala and Chyawanprash
plants.safety_notes: Very safe historically; high vitamin C may interact with chemotherapy antioxidant protocols (theoretical).
interactions: Theoretical: reduced absorption of some chemo agents
plants.gi_status: Nilgiri (Pudunagar) Amla holds a GI tag
plants.ip_notes: Neem-adjacent ayurvedic compositions containing amla are heavily TKDL-indexed; GI-tag value chain is a biodiversity benefit-sharing example.

traditional_uses: Skin disorders, wound cleansing, oral hygiene
plants.typical_dosage: Leaf churna 3-6 g/day; oil external only; seed oil NOT for internal use
plants.safety_notes: Neem oil ingestion is toxic, especially to children (hypoglycemia, encephalopathy). Avoid in pregnancy and infertility planning.
plants.ip_notes: The 2000 EPO revocation of the US/W.R. Grace fungicidal-neem patent (opposition led by India, Blaise Powell et al.) established 'traditional knowledge as prior art' in European practice.

plants.prabhava: Yogavahi (bio-enhancer carrying other drugs into tissue)
traditional_uses: Base resin of classical guggulu tablet formulations
plants.typical_dosage: Purified resin 300-600 mg standardized extract; classical shodhana required
plants.safety_notes: Unpurified guggulu contains heavy impurities - only shodhited material is pharmaceutical. Mild GI upset possible.
interactions: May reduce absorption of some drugs if not timed
plants.ip_notes: Multiple US patents on guggulipid for cholesterol were scrutinized against TKDL art; several claims narrowed during reexamination.

plants.prabhava: Yogavahi; central drug of vardhamana pippali karma (gradual rejuvenation protocol)
traditional_uses: Respirative tonic in shwasa and kasa
plants.typical_dosage: Powder 1-3 g/day; graduated pippali protocols only under guidance
plants.safety_notes: Pungent - avoid in active ulcers, bleeding disorders, excess pitta. Piperine inhibits CYP3A4/P-gp (drug interactions).
interactions: CYP3A4 and P-gp substrates (phenytoin, propranolol, etc.)
plants.ip_notes: Pippali as a bioenhancer is described in Charaka Samhita; TKDL citations have blocked modern patents claiming novel adjuvant use.

traditional_uses: External application for swelling and lymphatic congestion
plants.typical_dosage: Only in processed pharmaceutical doses (e.g., 125-250 mg in classical vatis); raw root is TOXIC
plants.safety_notes: TOXIC in overdose - plumbagin causes mucosal irritation, renal damage, hallucinations. Strictly contraindicated in pregnancy (abortifacient). Never self-dose.
plants.ip_notes: Aggressive toxicity profile means many western markets restrict it; Ayurvedic pharmacopoeial monographs (Schedule T) govern domestic manufacture.
